nodes.cesarz.text.t: "The Emperor? I think the world of him. Out loud, in front of anyone. Quietly I think something else, only you don't take quiet talk to a tavern, you take it to confession, and nobody round here has time for confession."

nodes.kurier.text.t: Grumble stops wiping the tankard, and that happens once a year. "They did. Only round here nobody asks straight out. They stand a round and wait for somebody's tongue to loosen. Nobody's loosened, because the beer was sour. But the next one who comes with gold instead of beer, I won't answer for."

nodes.nocleg.text.t: "Room upstairs, three groats a night, fleas thrown in free, 'cause there's no getting rid of them. Don't like it, the pigsty's warmer, but someone's already sleeping there and he doesn't share."

nodes.nocleg_ok.text.t: Grumble pockets the three groats with a knack any tax collector would be proud of. "Room upstairs, second door. If you hear rustling under the bed, it's not a mouse, it's my mother-in-law. She doesn't bite, she just talks."

nodes.plotki.text.t: Grumble leans over the counter. "Word is someone's been asking about survivors. Imperials, in red cloaks. Nobody knows a thing, because nobody saw a thing, and whoever did see is now very busy drinking his beer." The stonemasons from the Quarry below the hill, on the other hand, drink at his place from dawn till dark and brag that there's still plenty of stone to cut up there.

nodes.powitanie.options.[kurier].text.t: Anyone ask here about a courier in a red cloak?

nodes.powitanie.options.[nocleg].text.t: Where can a man get a night's sleep round here?

nodes.powitanie.options.[q2_zaplacil].te.t: Radosz paid. I've got your twelve groats.

nodes.powitanie.options.[q2_zwloka].text.t: Radosz asks for a week's grace.

nodes.powitanie.text.t: Grumble the innkeeper doesn't even get up from behind the counter. "New, are you? We don't like new faces here, but their coin's as good as anyone's. What'll it be? Gawking's free, mind, only you're scaring off my customers."

nodes.q2_start.text.t: Grumble wipes the counter. "Radosz the miller owes me twelve groats for beer he swilled back when he still had something to grind. Now the mill stands idle and Radosz pretends he doesn't know me. Go and see him, tell him I'm reminding him. If he pays, bring it here and you'll get a cut. Not the whole debt, just a crumb, 'cause I don't run a poorhouse."

nodes.q2_zaplacil.text.t: Grumble counts the coins twice, once by ear and once by tooth. "Twelve. A debtor paying up, that's a rare sight. Here's six for your trouble. Don't get used to it."

nodes.q2_zwloka.text.t: Grumble keeps quiet so long you start to regret opening your mouth. "A week. Fine. But if he doesn't pay, in a week you'll be paying me for his beer. I'm joking. Mostly." He turns back to his tankards, and a moment later tosses you six groats for your trouble, because, damn it all, he doesn't like owing anyone.
